_comment: Freeze manifest for the selected 10k VARIABLE-DT KalmanNet checkpoint. Written BEFORE any official AV2 VAL read (task section 17). Checkpoint selection used INTERNAL VALIDATION ONLY.

temporal_augmentation_policy.name: MILD-VARIABLE-DT
temporal_augmentation_policy.corruption_ordering: load clean -> temporal thinning -> GENERIC-ROBUST corruption on retained timesteps only

selection_provenance.selection_rationale: B (MILD) dominated on fixed+mild-dt internal-val eval and internal val loss (0.8288 vs C's 0.8867), and was within 0.24% of C on strong-dt eval, with fewer norm-overflow events. Section 15 criteria: (1) variable-dt validation improvement -- yes vs baseline A; (2) fixed-0.1 preservation -- best of the three at 2k; (3) numerical stability -- 1 overflow vs C's 2; (4) data retention -- 99.999% thinning applied. STRONG rejected for weaker overall.

dataset.note: 20 sequences (0.004%) too short to thin (n<2), dropped -- vs NATURAL baseline's 496434/57372; negligible.

optimizer_config.note: Frozen from the NATURAL 10k GENERIC-ROBUST baseline (PR #59 family). ONLY new axis vs baseline: temporal thinning (MILD policy). No architecture / hyperparameter retune.

comparison_to_natural_10k_seed1_baseline.finding: MILD temporal thinning did NOT increase numerical instability at 10k scale -- it had FEWER norm-overflow events (39 vs 78) and zero element-nonfinite events (vs 1) than the NATURAL FIXED-DT baseline. Section 21's concern about thinning producing harder gradients is not borne out for the MILD policy.

internal_val_dt_bucket_results._note: INTERNAL VAL only (9k/1k internal split). Official AV2 VAL results are added in a SEPARATE file AFTER this manifest is frozen.
internal_val_dt_bucket_results.interpretation: OUTCOME B (tradeoff): temporal-thinning training produces a monotonic dt-dependent tradeoff -- ~+1% position RMSE at dt=0.1s (worse), improving progressively to ~-3.2% position / ~-11% velocity RMSE at dt>=0.4s (better). Net effect is condition-dependent: -2.0% position under strong-thinning eval, +1.0% under fixed-dt eval, ~tie under mild-thinning eval. Magnitude is small. The 2k-screening signal (MILD beats baseline on all 3) did NOT fully hold at 10k -- the NATURAL 10k baseline is strong enough that variable-dt training only helps clearly in the heavier-thinning regime.
